title: Pure-Language Tree-Sitter Bash AST Parsing for Agent Shell Security Gates

claims.assertion: Pre-execution shell command permission policies must parse compound commands (pipes, subshells, redirects, chained operators) into full Tree-Sitter AST nodes using pure managed-language parsers to prevent native C-addon build failures across host environments

context: Regular expression and simple whitespace splitting fail on complex shell commands involving subshells `$(...)`, environment variable prefixes `FOO=bar rm -rf /`, chained commands `cmd1 && cmd2`, or process substitutions `<(...)`, enabling malicious command injection or bypass of agent safety guardrails. Furthermore, native C bindings for Tree-Sitter fail to compile in minimal Docker/serverless environments.
distilled_learning: Implement or adopt a pure-managed language (TypeScript / Python) port of the Tree-Sitter Bash grammar that outputs 1:1 identical AST nodes (`command`, `pipeline`, `subshell`, `redirect`, `declaration_command`). Traverse the AST to decompose compound pipelines into individual executable units and analyze arguments, variables, and flags deterministically against security permission policies (`allow`, `deny`, `ask_user`).
